title: Consistent analytics replay bridge with staleness SLA and tenant soft-pin controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a pluggable 'replay bridge' service for console analytics that enables ordered, consistent replication of tenant usage events across regions while enforcing per-tenant soft-pin (time-to-live) residency policies and a defined staleness SLA. This ticket covers the backend bridge, control-plane endpoints for pinning/evacuation, and the incremental replay engine used during cross-region rehoming and DR drills.

Background: Existing analytics pipeline copies streams to multiple regions but lacks a deterministic replay mechanism for staged tenant evacuation and does not expose per-tenant soft-pinning from the Console. Customers on Dedicated/Private deployments require controlled rehoming with bounded staleness and auditability. The bridge will be used for: 1) planned tenant region reassignments, 2) emergency evacuation playbooks, and 3) cross-region DR rehearsal without impacting live write paths.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement long-term archival or full-schema migration tooling, and does not change the live write affinity codepaths for token-gated routing.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge service can subscribe to primary analytics topic and produce ordered deltas to target region replicas with preserved event ordering per-tenant.
Per-tenant soft-pin API exposed on Console control-plane: pin(duration), release(), query_status() and returns residency metadata and last-replay-offset.
Staleness SLA enforcement: 95th percentile end-to-end replay lag <= 60s under normal load for tenants flagged medium-to-high locality.
Evacuation staging mode: support dry-run (replay-only) and cutover (replay + redirect) with audit log entries and rollback hooks.
Automated tests and an integration test harness that simulates regional network partitions and validates consistency and ordered delivery across regions.
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (replay_lag_seconds, replay_errors_total, soft_pin_count) and dashboards in Console show per-tenant replay lag and state.
Security review completed and KMS keys used for metadata encryption in transit and at rest for the bridge control plane.
Documentation: design doc and runbook checked into Confluence and a short how-to in Console docs for operations and customer-facing guidance.
tech_decisions: Keep the bridge as an idempotent, single-writer per-tenant consumer to preserve ordering; use at-least-once semantics with deterministic de-duplication via (tenant_id, event_seq).
Use bounded in-memory journal + on-disk segment store for replay buffering to avoid blocking on transient target-region backpressure.
Soft-pin policy is enforced in the control plane (Console backend) and propagated as a per-tenant header to the bridge; runtime checks in bridge reject replay to non-authorized regions.

Trade-off: Strong ordering guarantees increase latency for high-throughput tenants; we will mitigate by sharding tenants across bridge workers and using continuous compaction to reduce duplicate processing.
We will use the existing message transport (Kafka topic namespaces) but add a small envelope for replay metadata to keep compatibility with downstream analytics consumers.
Rollout strategy: start with a small pilot of 5 tenants (low-risk) in staging, measure replay lag and operational overhead, then expand to a beta cohort.
work_items: Design: finalize replay envelope format and on-disk journal layout (confluence doc).
API: add Console control-plane endpoints for pin/release/status and RBAC checks.
Bridge: implement ordered consumer, local journal, and target-producer with backpressure-aware retry logic.
Replay Engine: implement offset checkpointing and idempotent apply at target region ingestion layer.
Integration tests: simulate partitions, topology failover, and assert staleness SLA.
Metrics & Alerts: instrument replay_lag_seconds (p50/p95), add pager rule if p95 > 120s for pilot tenants.
Docs & Runbook: write DR drill steps and rollback procedure for Console operators.
Security: KMS integration for metadata encryption and produce security review package.
QA: coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer-facing validation on Dedicated instances.
Deployment: canary deploy bridge in us-west-2 then roll to eu-west-1 after 1 week of stability.
Postmortem template: prepare incident playbook for replay divergence, include replay verification commands.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting held with Console, Analytics, and Platform teams. Agreed on pilot tenant selection criteria and staleness SLA target (p95 <= 60s). (Aisha)
2026-02-20: Prototype of on-disk journal sketched; opted for LSM-like segment layout to allow fast tail reads. Initial benchmark shows ~30ms tail-read per segment under synthetic load. (Marco)
2026-02-28: Control-plane API schema PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2145. Awaiting PM review for RBAC labels and telemetry hooks. (Marco)
2026-03-04: Decided to reuse analytics-kafka namespace for initial pilot to minimize infra changes; added replay envelope version header for compatibility. (Aisha)

2026-03-09: Integration harness prototype passes ordered delivery tests for 10k events/tenant; observed occasional duplicate delivery when target backpressure spikes — added deterministic dedupe by event_seq. (Marco)
2026-03-12: Security review kickoff scheduled; prepping KMS key policy doc and threat model for metadata and replay control plane. Beta rollout pushed to 2026-03-24 to allow for remediation. (Aisha)
2026-03-12: Updated acceptance criteria to include explicit audit log entries for evacuation and dry-run mode results. (Aisha)
metrics: Target error rate replay_errors_total < 0.5% under 99th percentile load
Soft-pin enforcement success ratio = 100% for pinned tenants during pilot
Disk journal read throughput >= 5000 events/s per worker
notes: Operational concern: ensure bridge does not become a single point of failure — design will allow stateless replicas with externalized checkpoint store (S3-compatible) as follow-up.
Customer communication: prepare a short FAQ for Dedicated customers describing the soft-pin feature and evacuation semantics.
Follow-up tickets: introduce 'auto-evacuation-scheduler' to schedule cross-region rehoming windows with SLA guardrails (TBD).
